svg.title: Eventhouse and KQL Database Architecture
svg.desc: An architecture diagram showing streaming ingestion into Eventhouse KQL databases, separating premium hot cache from retained storage, and exposing data through native KQL and OneLake Delta availability.
svg.text: Streaming Ingestion · Hot SSD Cache vs Retained History · OneLake Delta Mirroring · Multi-Engine Analytics

g.title: Streaming sources — Real-Time Intelligence discovers and routes event data.
g.text: Continuous event feeds shaped and routed into KQL storage
• Ingestion batching & streaming ingestion policies tune latency vs throughput
• Automatic schema detection and mapping for JSON, Parquet, CSV, and raw text logs.

g.title: Eventhouse container — Eventhouse groups KQL databases under shared resources and monitoring.
g.text: Workspace container grouping KQL databases under shared compute & telemetry
• Dynamic resource allocation: Busy databases utilize spare capacity from idle ones.
• System Overview dashboard aggregates cross-database CPU, memory & ingestion metrics.

svg.text: KQL DATABASE INTERNAL STORAGE & CACHING TIERS

g.title: KQL retained data — Retention policy governs the full queryable history.
g.text: • Data organized by physical arrival time
• Fast time-slice slicing across billions of rows
• Dynamic JSON columns indexed in flight
• Configurable from hours to decades (e.g. 365 days)
• Cold data resides on cost-effective persistent store
• Data remains 100% queryable via standard KQL
Warning: Reducing retention permanently drops data
and removes aged records from OneLake Delta mirror.

g.title: Premium hot cache — Caching policy keeps a recent window on premium storage.
g.text: • Hot cache window (e.g. last 7 days or 30 days)
• Uncompressed column chunks pinned in RAM/SSD
• Powers live incident response & NOC dashboards
• Zero disk spin-up or cold-storage fetch delay
• Hot cache sizing controls capacity unit consumption
• Queries automatically span hot + cold seamlessly
Optimization Tip: Keep only actively queried
operational windows hot to preserve CU budget.

g.title: OneLake availability — Optional availability exposes KQL tables as Delta to other engines.
g.text: • Automatically writes Delta Lake Parquet tables
• Direct Lake semantic models read with 0 ETL
while OneLake availability is actively enabled.
• Disable ➔ Modify DDL ➔ Re-enable triggers backfill.
balances file size vs downstream freshness.

g.title: Query consumers — KQL serves native analytics while OneLake enables other engines.
g.text: Unified query execution across native KQL and cross-engine OneLake readers
• Evaluates against Hot SSD & Retained tiers
• Reads Delta mirror in OneLake directly
• 0 import schedule or model size bloat
Use Native KQL for sub-second telemetry exploration & time-series anomalies; use Direct Lake & Spark over OneLake Delta
when joining streaming history against dimensional master data curated in Warehouse or Lakehouse.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Eventhouse & KQL Database Specs.
